name: Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex Due to BP230 Deficiency
aliases: Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex with BP230 mutation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex Due to BP230 Deficiency

criteria.description: Presence of skin blistering localized to basal keratinocytes, typically on hands and feet, triggered by minor trauma
Immunofluorescence microscopy showing absent or markedly reduced BP230 protein expression in basal keratinocytes
Identification of pathogenic variants in the DST gene encoding BP230 by molecular genetic testing
Skin biopsy demonstrating intraepidermal cleavage at the basal layer

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of typical clinical blistering plus either immunofluorescence evidence of BP230 deficiency or pathogenic DST gene mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires correlation of clinical, immunopathological, and genetic findings.

pathognomonic.notes: Blisters typically form on hands and feet after minor mechanical stress
searchTerms: blisters forming at base skin layer after injury
skin blisters from trauma at basal layer

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absent or markedly reduced BP230 protein expression in basal keratinocytes
searchTerms: lack of key skin protein in basal cells
missing BP230 protein in skin cells

common.symptomName: Non-scarring skin erosions following blister rupture
searchTerms: skin sores that don't scar after blisters break

common.notes: Thickened skin areas due to chronic friction
searchTerms: thickened skin on hands and feet
hardened skin on hands and feet

common.notes: Nail abnormalities such as ridging or thickening

common.symptomName: Blistering exacerbated by heat or sweating
common.notes: Increased blister formation in warm environments
searchTerms: blistering worsened by heat or sweat

occasional.notes: Less frequent involvement of mucous membranes
Darkened skin patches following lesion healing

rare.notes: Rare hair loss due to scalp blistering
Excessive sweating of palms and soles
searchTerms: excessive sweating on palms and soles
increased sweat in hands and feet

laboratory: Immunofluorescence microscopy showing absent or reduced BP230 staining
Histopathology revealing intraepidermal cleavage at basal keratinocytes
other: Clinical observation of trauma-induced blistering localized to basal epidermis

distinguishingFeatures: Mutations in keratin 5 or 14 genes instead of DST
Blistering primarily intraepidermal but with normal BP230 expression
Blistering occurs at lamina lucida of basement membrane zone
Immunofluorescence shows normal BP230 but reduced laminin-332 or integrin expression

redFlags: Delayed wound healing with signs of systemic infection
Unexplained mucosal involvement or airway compromise
references: Fine JD, et al. Inherited epidermolysis bullosa: updated recommendations on diagnosis and classification. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2021.
